**Alpha.** An early look at tempo and time signature in Silly MIDI Tools: a native macOS app that turns audio into MIDI. It is unsigned, and parts of it have only been checked by automated tests. Expect rough edges, and please report them.

## What's new since 0.6.3

MIDI files now carry a tempo and a time signature that you choose, and the app helps you find them.

- **You set the tempo and time signature.** A new recording starts from Settings, General, which holds 120 BPM in 4/4 until you change it. The Audio inspector's **Tempo** section and the MIDI editor have the same fields: tempo in quarter notes per minute, beats per bar and the beat note. **Add meter change** switches the meter at any bar. The roll, the waveform's bar lines, the bar.beat readout and the saved file all follow the grid. A file holds one tempo.
- **The notes never move.** Changing the tempo or the meter changes the grid and the file's ticks, not when a note sounds, so the notes stay in time with the audio.
- **Click.** A woodblock plays on every beat, higher on beat 1 of each bar. Use the Click button in the transport, Controls, Click, or the **C** key.
- **Tempo from your notes.** After a run, the inspector ranks up to three tempos by how well the notes fall on a sixteenth-note grid, and marks half and double time.
- **Tempo from the audio.** **Detect from audio** suggests a tempo, a bar 1 and a meter map. A quick estimate works out of the box. The optional **Beat This!** helper (82 MB, a download button in the Tempo section or in Settings, Models, Helpers) finds beats and downbeats, draws them on the waveform and says whether the tempo is steady.
- **Check alignment.** After a run, it says what share of the notes sit on an audio onset and how early or late they are. It never moves a note.
- **Nothing is applied until you press Use.** Every suggestion is yours to take, and each one is a single undo step.
- **Import and export** read and write the tempo and every time signature.

## Known limits

- This is an alpha. The automated tests pass (404 tests), but the screens were not driven by hand: the click, the meter-change editing, the waveform's beat lines and the Beat This! download flow need your eyes.
- Release builds are Apple silicon only, and are not notarized. The arm64 app itself has not been run by hand.
- A song whose tempo changes has to be transcribed in sections. Importing a file converts its later tempo changes into real time.
- Beat This! can be unsure about downbeats, and half and double time are both valid for most music. Treat the suggestions as readings, not facts.
- Beat This! is downloaded from Hugging Face (`thebluescreen/beat-this-onnx`) the first time you ask for it. Nothing is downloaded before that.
